title: Hedge prediction stays in the convex prediction set
statement: Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set, fix any learning rate $\eta \in \bbr$, a loss function $\ell : \bbr \to \Omega \to \bbr$, expert predictions $p_t(i)$, and a sequence of outcomes, and suppose that every expert prediction lies in $S$, that is $p_t(i) \in S$ for all rounds $t$ and all experts $i$. Then for every round $t$, Hedge's weighted-average prediction $\widehat{x}_t = \sum_{i} w^{(\eta)}_{t,i}\, p_t(i)$ — formed from the Hedge distribution of the loss table induced by $\ell$, the predictions, and the outcomes up to round $t$ — again lies in $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $\widehat{x}_t$ is the Hedge weighted-average prediction at round $t$
replaced:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a convex set and suppose every expert prediction
satisfies $p_t(i) \in S$ for all $t$ and $i$.  Then Hedge's weighted-average
prediction $\widehat{x}_t \in S$ for every round $t$.  The result follows because
the Hedge weights are nonneg\-ative and sum to one, so the weighted average is a
convex combination of points in $S$.
